chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a female slave who entered into a contract of manumission (mukatabah) and had paid two-thirds of the agreed amount, and it had been stipulated upon her that if she became unable to pay, she would return to slavery. We were in a state of freedom regarding what we had taken from her, and two installments (najm) had become due upon her. He said: 'She is returned [to slavery], and it is pleasing to them [the master] regarding what they had taken from her.' And he said: 'She does not have the right to delay the installment after its due date by one month, except with their permission.'

key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a fixed sum for freedom

ai.seo_question: What happens to a contractual slave who misses an installment payment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of a *mukatab* (contractual slave) who defaults on the final third of her manumission price, ruling that she reverts to slavery while the master retains the paid portion as compensation. It further establishes a strict procedural limit, prohibiting the slave from delaying any installment beyond one month without the master's explicit consent, thereby balancing contractual obligation with practical flexibility. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the binding nature of the *kitabah* contract and the conditions under which manumission is revoked due to inability to pay.
